Expectation1: Fix bugs and troubleshoot issues reported by users or QA
Situation1: Several users report intermittent errors that disrupt normal usage
Expectation2: Support individuals or groups in accessing essential services and resources
Situation2: They encounter a situation where someone urgently needs housing, medical help, or protection and must be connected to services quickly.
Story: I stared at my screen, the error logs scrolling faster than I could read. Users were reporting intermittent bugs—some couldn’t log in, others lost their work mid-session. My team was counting on me to find the root cause and patch it before the next release. The pressure was mounting; every minute the issue persisted, more users were affected. My phone buzzed. It was a message from the shelter coordinator: a young woman and her child needed immediate housing and medical attention. If I didn’t act now, they might be left on the street tonight. My mind raced. As a developer, I was expected to drop everything and fix the bugs, but as an advocate, I couldn’t ignore someone in crisis. Both roles demanded my full attention, both were urgent, and both carried consequences if I failed. My hands hovered over the keyboard, torn between two worlds, feeling the weight of responsibility pressing in from all sides.
